newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Russia says treaty needed to protect forests.
newsitem.headline: Russia says treaty needed to protect forests.

text.p: With a fifth of the world's trees within his borders, Russian President Victor Chernomyrdin called on Monday for a treaty to protect the world's forests, calling them the "lungs of the planet."

"Russia attaches great significance to rational use and conservation of forests for the needs of succeeding generations and the whole of mankind," he told a U.N. Earth Summit discussing ways to protect the environment.
"We believe the time has come for an early initiation of negotiations for development of an international legal instrument on forests." he said.

Canada has long advocated a convention on forests and is backed by the European Union, Malaysia and Costa Rica. The United States, Brazil and India are opposed, as are most environmental groups, which believe a conference would give major logging states an excuse to maintain current policies.
Russia still has vast areas of forest, mainly in Siberia, that play a vital role in climate regulation by absorbing damaging carbon emissions.

But some experts believe Siberia is losing 4 million hectares (9.8 million acres) of forest annually, nearly twice the rate of deforestation in Brazil, as local and foreign companies rush to cut down trees.
Russia is also the third largest producer of carbon dioxide, the key greenhouse gas that causes global warming, and has done little to reduce emissions.
But because of the collapse of its energy-intensive industries, its emissions fell 28 percent between 1990 and 1995.
